title: Towards End-to-End Learning of Protein Structure Prediction and Structure-based Sequence Design
experiments_summary: The paper trains and evaluates E2EFOLD, a discrete stochastic protein structure autoencoder that jointly learns structure-based sequence design (encoder) and structure prediction of designed sequences (decoder). The encoder is based on ProteinMPNN with an added attention layer and simultaneous (non-autoregressive) residue prediction. The decoder is a downsized ESMFold architecture without the protein language model, with an increased number of recycling iterations and a modified structure module for all-atom coordinate reconstruction. Discrete sequences are sampled differentiably using the Gumbel-Softmax trick with straight-through gradient estimation. The model is trained with a composite loss combining FAPE, Cα-FAPE, torsion, distogram, and sequence recovery terms. Two datasets are used: (1) CATH 4.2 splits from Ingraham et al. for training and evaluation, and (2) E2EData, a custom dataset curated from the Protein Data Bank (PDB) filtered by resolution ≤3 Å, sequence lengths 50–412 residues, excluding homooligomers, and clustered with foldseek-multimer into 90/5/5 train/validation/test splits. A third dataset, RFData, consisting of RFDiffusion-generated backbones, is used for evaluation only. Sequence design is assessed by sequence recovery (cross-entropy-based) and self-consistency (TM-score and RMSD between the reference structure and Boltz-2 predictions of designed sequences). Structure prediction is assessed by RMSD to the reference structure, with Boltz-2 used as the reference baseline method. An ablation study removes the structural loss terms to quantify their contribution to self-consistency. Experiments are conducted across multiple protein length ranges to examine how performance scales with sequence length.
